To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

hemicelluloselike molecules can be incorporated into bacterial cellulose to produce celluloses with a more ordered structure and that the coaggregation and occlusion of these hemicellulose molecules with cellulose may be a mechanism by which the hemicellulosesstructure cellulose in higher plants.
hemicellulosic molecules are incorporated into the cellulose microfibrils and affect their aggregation in vitro and in vivo.

the addition of hemicellulosic polymers to cellulose cultures of Acetobacter xylimum resulted in cellulose with a more ordered structure and a greater degree of aggregation, and that this effect is likely to be due to the hemicelluloselocating within and between the cellulose crystallites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new cellulose-based materials.
the structure and function of the cellulosic materials that occur in nature.
the structure and chemistry of the cell wall polysaccharides of higher plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cellulose microfibril is the fundamental structural unit of all plant cell wall systems and that the hemicellulosic components are the primary moderators of the microfibril's properties.

the cellulose microfibrils in higher plants are not randomly oriented and that they are not randomly associated with one another in cell walls; rather, they are organized into bundles that may be as much as 10 times the diameter of a single fibril.
the hemicellulosic polymers, in the presence of cellulose, are involved in the aggregation of celluloses into a variety of morphologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hemicellulosic polymers are structure regulators in cellulose aggregation.
the hemicellulosic polysaccharide is a structure regulator for the native cellulose of the higher plant cell wall.

hemicellulosic polymers can be regarded as structure regulators in plant cell walls, and that they are able to influence the properties of the cell wall by their ability to control the aggregation of celluloses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the structure of the cell wall is not a simple reflection of the properties of its components, but rather that the properties of the cell wall are the result of interactions between its components, and that the interactions are themselves a reflection of the biological function of the cell wall.
the hemicellulosic matrix is a key regulator of cellulose structure in higher plant cell wall.
the structure of the cellulose is not only determined by the cellulose itself.
